content_of_post_to_answer: How do I come up with a strong enough "why" to successfully change my habits?
answer: A strong “why” is often misunderstood as finding a dramatic purpose that makes change effortless. In reality, many lasting changes begin when the cost of staying the same becomes clearer than the discomfort of changing. A person may not need a grand vision; they may need an honest connection between a daily habit and the kind of life it is quietly creating. Motivation fades, but a clear understanding of what a habit is protecting or damaging can keep guiding decisions when emotions are absent.
